entities.summary: Salome, Op. 54, is an opera in one act by Richard Strauss, dedicated to his friend Sir Edgar Speyer. The libretto is Hedwig Lachmann's German translation of Oscar Wilde's 1891 French play Salomé, edited by the composer. Strauss was inspired by Wilde's exploration of themes such as desire, power, and the blurring of moral boundaries. The opera premiered in 1905 and has since become a landmark of modernist opera, its complex characters and symbolism continuing to fascinate audiences. Its influence can be seen in the works of later composers, such as Alban Berg and Pierre Boulez, who were drawn to its innovative use of atonality and its exploration of the human condition. The opera's legacy extends beyond the world of opera, with its themes and characters continuing to resonate in contemporary culture, from film and literature to art and fashion. Despite its relatively short history, Salome has become an iconic work of modernist art, its influence still felt today in the world of music and beyond.
